Signal-Based GTM: From Market Signals to
Coordinated Outreach
Leadnius GTM Resource
A practical framework for connecting buying signals, account enrichment, prioritisation, personalised
messaging, and coordinated outreach.
Why traditional outbound breaks down
Many outbound teams begin with large scraped lists and generic messaging. This can create
disconnected research, weak prioritisation, repetitive manual work, and limited visibility into why an
account was contacted.
• 
Lists are collected without enough account or buyer context.
• 
The same message is reused across different personas and situations.
• 
Sales teams spend time researching and moving information between tools.
• 
Signals such as funding, hiring, technology changes, website activity, or product triggers are not
consistently connected to outreach.
• 
Reporting arrives after activity instead of helping the team decide what to do next.
A signal-based GTM motion
A signal-based model connects signals to enrichment, scoring, messaging, orchestration, and CRM
intelligence. The goal is to turn a relevant signal into a clear next action for the revenue team.
1. Capture signals
Track events that can indicate a change in account relevance or buying context, including funding
announcements, hiring activity, technology-stack changes, website visits, and product-related triggers.
2. Enrich the account
Add the information needed to understand the account and the people involved. A waterfall approach
can check another data source when the previous provider cannot supply the required information.
3. Prioritise accounts
Combine fit and intent signals to decide where the team should spend attention first. Criteria can include
ICP, target persona, geography, account characteristics, and buying signals.
4. Build relevant messaging
Use account and buyer context to create messaging for the relevant persona. Personalisation should be
based on real signals rather than superficial variables in a generic template.
5. Orchestrate the motion
Connect enrichment and prioritisation to outreach and CRM processes. Automation should reduce
repetitive execution while keeping appropriate human control over important decisions.

6. Keep CRM intelligence current
Account and activity intelligence should remain connected to the systems the revenue team uses so
sales and marketing can act on current information.
Leadnius approach
Leadnius describes its GTM engineering approach around deep enrichment, persona-specific
messaging, fit and intent scoring, automated orchestration, and live visibility. Its GTM engineering
service describes a flow from signal to enrichment to scoring and coordinated outreach.
Implementation checklist
• 
Define the ICP and target personas.
• 
Choose the account and buyer signals that matter.
• 
Set enrichment rules and fallback data sources.
• 
Define fit and intent scoring criteria.
• 
Create messaging frameworks for important personas.
• 
Connect the workflow to the existing CRM and outreach stack.
• 
Define human approval points for high-impact actions.
• 
Create dashboards for current GTM activity and account status.
• 
Review signal quality and routing rules regularly.
Conclusion
A signal-based GTM system is less about sending more messages and more about deciding which
accounts deserve attention, why they deserve it, and what the team should do next.

Case Study: Building a Signal-Based GTM
Workflow
Leadnius — Illustrative Workflow Case Study
This is an illustrative case study for testing the Leadnius resource workflow. It describes a representative GTM workflow and
does not claim results for a named customer.
The challenge
A B2B revenue team wanted a structured way to identify accounts worth contacting and turn relevant
signals into coordinated sales activity. The existing process depended on manual research, separate
data sources, generic outreach, and repeated CRM updates.
The operating requirements
• 
Identify accounts using meaningful market and buyer signals.
• 
Enrich accounts and contacts with useful context.
• 
Prioritise accounts using fit and intent.
• 
Create messaging that reflects the target persona and available context.
• 
Coordinate outreach without manually moving information between systems.
• 
Maintain visibility into account status and GTM activity.
The Leadnius workflow
Stage 01 — Signal
Relevant signals can include funding, hiring, technology changes, website activity, and product-related
triggers. These signals provide the context for deciding which accounts should enter the GTM workflow.
Stage 02 — Enrich
Accounts are enriched with company and buyer information. A waterfall approach can fill missing fields
by moving to another provider when the previous source does not return the required data.
Stage 03 — Score
Accounts are prioritised using fit and intent. The scoring model can incorporate ICP criteria, persona
relevance, geography, company characteristics, and the strength of available buying signals.
Stage 04 — Message
Account and persona context shapes relevant messaging. Instead of treating every prospect the same,
content reflects why the account entered the workflow and the role being contacted.
Stage 05 — Orchestrate
Qualified accounts move into the appropriate outreach and CRM processes. Automation handles
repeatable execution while the team retains control over actions that require human judgement.

Stage 06 — Measure
Live visibility is maintained across account status, workflow activity, and GTM execution, giving the team
a way to review and improve the workflow.
What this workflow changes
• 
From large undifferentiated lists to prioritised accounts.
• 
From generic outreach to persona-aware messaging.
• 
From disconnected research to a connected workflow.
• 
From manual handoffs to coordinated orchestration.
• 
From delayed reporting to current GTM visibility.
Where Leadnius fits
Leadnius positions its GTM engineering offering around signal capture, deep enrichment, fit and intent
scoring, persona-specific messaging, orchestration, and live dashboards. This workflow reflects those
capabilities without inventing customer-specific performance claims.
Takeaway
The value of a signal-based GTM workflow comes from connecting the full chain: identify the signal,
understand the account, decide its priority, create relevant messaging, coordinate the next action, and
keep the resulting intelligence visible to the team.
